name: Before, After, Bridge
summary: Show the painful before, the desirable after, then present the solution as the bridge between them.
references: Copywriting formula popularized in direct-response marketing; see Joanna Wiebe, Copyhackers (2010s)

sequence.purpose: Before: the world with the problem.
Put before and after side by side.
Bridge: what gets you from before to after.
Show the bridge is easy to cross.

pitfalls: A before the audience does not recognize as theirs.
An after that is vague or unbelievable.
A bridge that looks harder than the problem.

example.topic: A fictional invoicing tool for small agencies
outline: Before: invoices chased by phone every Friday
After: invoices paid before you think of them
The bridge: reminders that send themselves
Connect your ledger, pick a schedule, done
Start a free month this week
